bullets.title: 10Y yield breaks 5%, Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75-4%; more hikes expected
bullets.body: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.0% in a unanimous decision during the week, with Chair Warsh signaling 'unwavering' commitment to price stability. The 10-year Treasury yield broke above 5% for the first time since 2007 (touched 5.027%), and Goldman now expects another hike in October. Prediction markets price 84-87% probability of at least one more hike in 2026, with futures implying ~90bp of additional tightening through Q1 2027.

bullets.title: Wage growth re-acceleration + labor market tightness supports hawkish Fed
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro data shows Initial Claims fell to 196k—near multi-decade lows—with Continuing Claims at 1.73M (-10% YoY). ADP data shows re-firming hiring; Indeed Job Postings turning positive for first time post-pandemic. Regional Fed surveys show wages and workweek hours rising, small business hiring plans near highs. September CPI nowcast raised to 3.61% y/y, reinforcing inflation staying above target.

bullets.title: U.S. 2-year yield hits highest since July 2024 at 4.76%; 1-year forward 2s top 5%
bullets.body: Short-end yields surged on hawkish Fed messaging and strong economic data: the 2-year hit 4.76% (highest since July 2024), while the 1-year forward 2s rate broke above 5%. Yield curve continues to flatten with the 10s-2s spread compressed to roughly 28bp, signaling the market is pricing the best of the growth cycle as behind.

bullets.title: Equity market regime: tech/AI stable, semis bifurcating; S&P near TREND support
bullets.body: The week was marked by a sharp Software-over-Semis rotation—the pair hit its largest single-day spread in history (+12.5%) after Anthropic CEO called for slowing frontier AI development. SPX held key support at 7,500-7,600 but Hedgeye flagged bearish TRADE signals; Goldman warned CTAs are positioned as sellers across all scenarios next week. Shiller CAPE at 40.3 and US market-to-GDP at 240% (well above dot-com's 150%) represent extreme valuations.

bullets.title: AI safety/pacing debate reshapes sector rotation; Anthropic targets November IPO
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to 'pace' frontier AI development—backed by Musk and Altman—triggered a massive rotation: SOX -5.9%, Software +3.2-5%, cybersecurity names (CRWD, PANW) +10-15%. NVDA CEO Jensen Huang and Trump publicly dismissed the slowdown thesis. Anthropic pushed its IPO target to November (from October), and prediction markets price only a 6% chance of Anthropic going public by month-end.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex remains intact; AI safety actually requires MORE compute
bullets.body: Citi AI Infrastructure Summit Day 1 showed Nvidia, Broadcom, and Meta management all dismissing slowdown fears: AVGO CEO reaffirmed $115B FY27 AI revenue target; NVDA CEO stated chip sales will double next year. AI alignment and safety monitoring add an estimated 20% incremental compute overhead, net bullish for GPU demand. Goldman estimates $420B of hyperscaler gross debt issuance in 2027 (+60% vs. 2026).

bullets.title: Middle East geopolitical risk: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Hormuz flows near zero
bullets.body: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was struck by Houthi drones (offline for weeks), forcing crude rerouting through Hormuz—where tanker crossings crashed to 4/day vs. a 10-day average of 16 and pre-war ~135/day. Dated Brent closed the week near $130/bbl; WTI briefly broke $100 but pulled back to $103. Saudi Arabia suspended crude allocations to European refiners for October; Saudi Aramco fuel tanks near Riyadh Airport were also struck. Iran's blockade of its own oil exports is confirmed by CENTCOM.

bullets.title: Oil and energy driving inflation; US diesel, jet fuel at record highs
bullets.body: US diesel hit an all-time high of $6.40-6.45/gallon (AAA); jet fuel prices returned to Iran-War highs; national average gas hit $6.31/gallon (EIA). Brent crude settled ~$103-106/bbl. US refiners ran at 97% capacity. Southwest and major carriers canceled December flights on fuel costs; United Airlines canceling December capacity. France is running out of fuel with 11% of stations nationwide out of stock.

bullets.title: BOJ hikes to 1.25% (31-year high) but yen weakens on dovish dissents
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised its overnight call rate by 25bp to 1.25%, the highest since 1995, in a 7-2 vote. The two dissents were interpreted as dovish, sending USD/JPY sharply higher (above 157 at points). Governor Ueda emphasized rate-hike pace will be data-dependent and cautioned against excessive tightening speed. Citigroup now forecasts BoJ hikes in December, March, and July 2027.

bullets.title: France credit downgraded to A+ by Scope; French 10Y yield at 2008 high, OAT-Bund spread at 100bp
bullets.body: Scope downgraded France's sovereign rating to A+ from AA-, and France's 10-year bond yield climbed to 4.56%—the highest since 2008—with the spread over German Bunds widening to 100bp (first time since 2012). France's 2026 deficit forecast was revised up to 5.4% and debt-to-GDP is projected to reach 119.3% by 2026. European equities saw broad pressure with DAX breaking key technical support.

bullets.title: Global housing/macro: US housing sellers at 6-year high with 58% more sellers than buyers
bullets.body: Redfin data showed 1.53M sellers vs. 972K buyers in August—a 58% imbalance, the biggest mismatch since 2013. Pending home sales moved deeper into negative YoY territory. Multifamily housing starts collapsed 22% MoM in August, and NAHB sentiment hit its lowest since 2022. US 30-year mortgage rates reached 7.24%.

bullets.title: Trump announces AI Force and AI Czar; projects AI at 25% of US GDP; US-Denmark Greenland deal
bullets.body: Trump announced the creation of an 'AI Force' modeled on Space Force and plans for an AI Czar, projecting AI could reach 25% of US GDP. Separately, the US, Denmark, and Greenland signed a security agreement expanding Washington's Arctic presence. Trump also signed the Russia sanctions bill (Lindsey Graham Act) and announced MFN drug pricing for all 50-state Medicaid programs.

bullets.title: US economic data: August industrial production flat vs +0.3% expected; LEI -0.1%
bullets.body: August industrial production came in flat MoM vs. +0.3% consensus; manufacturing fell 0.3% vs. +0.3% expected. The Conference Board's Leading Economic Index declined 0.1% vs. +0.1% estimate. Capacity utilization hit 76.3% vs. 76.4% expected. Philadelphia Fed ISM-adjusted index fell to 58.3 in September (still expansionary). All three releases missed estimates.

bullets.title: Semiconductor supply tightening: memory prices surged 5-7x; DRAM 512GB DDR5 module debuted
bullets.body: Intel CEO flagged memory prices up 5-7x with shortage expected to worsen through 2027; SK Hynix labeled 2027 as potentially the worst supply year. Micron successfully demonstrated the world's first 512GB DDR5 module (volume production targeting 2H 2027). Apple accepted Samsung's memory price hikes for 1Q27. Wolfe's semiconductor inventory analysis showed 58 days (+4 days q/q), flashing a yellow flag.

bullets.title: Meta Muse hits #1 on Apple App Store, overtaking ChatGPT
bullets.body: Meta's new AI agent app Muse reached the #1 spot on the US Apple App Store free apps rankings, surpassing ChatGPT. It accumulated 900K+ downloads in the first week. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated 100M Muse users could add 1% to 2028 EPS, with 15%+ upside if transaction monetization materializes. Meta also launched a tiered Meta One subscription service starting at $2.99/month.

bullets.title: Bond market: $625B record flows into US bond funds YTD; record $7T quad-witching expiry
bullets.body: US bond funds attracted $625B in the first 8 months of 2026—an all-time high—signaling significant investor rotation toward fixed income. Separately, Friday's quad-witching event involved $7 trillion in notional value (2nd largest ever), with $5.2B SPY put wall at 760 notable ahead of expiry. Goldman's panic index saw its largest 1-day decline in 10 years after the peak of volatility.

bullets.title: OpenAI projects $280B cash burn through 2030; revenue target $350B but expenses far exceed
bullets.body: The Financial Times reported OpenAI forecasts $278-280B in negative free cash flow from 2026-2030, with the company potentially exhausting capital by 2028 without additional fundraising. OpenAI projects revenue scaling from $36B to $350B by 2030, but operating expenses far outpace revenues. OpenAI is reportedly in early talks for a private round at $1.2T valuation, and its IPO was delayed to at least 2027.

bullets.title: Goldman: AI capex tailwind to S&P earnings will fade in 2027-28 as depreciation mounts
bullets.body: Goldman's chief US equity strategist noted AI capex currently drives nearly 50% of S&P 500 earnings growth, but this tailwind is expected to diminish next year. The firm's model estimates AI investment transitions from an +11pp earnings tailwind in 2026 to a marginal drag in 2028 as depreciation builds. S&P 500 is described as 'over-earning but not in a bubble,' with 11% EPS growth forecast for 2027.

bullets.title: ECB signals December hike; BoE set to hike November; Western European central banks turning hawkish in unison
bullets.body: JPMorgan now expects the ECB to deliver a fourth hike in March 2027, with December as the natural timing for the next move, as Eurozone headline inflation is forecast to reach 3.9% by 4Q26 and core to peak at 2.7% in 1Q27. The BoE held at 3.75% but delivered hawkish guidance signaling a November hike, with CPI accelerating to 3.1% in August and forecast to peak near 4% by early 2027. All major DM central banks (Fed, BOJ, ECB, BoE) tightened in the same month for the first time.
